 JUDGMENT Petitioner asserting to be an injured suffered in a RTA filed application under Section 166 of M.V.Act claiming compensation worth of Rs.18,00,000/- from the respondents, who are the insurer and owner of Bus bearing No.KA-40-6834, asserting that on 27.05.2022 at 7.45 a.m. when riding motorcycle bearing No.KA-40-H- 7445 from Anemadagu towards Talakayalabetta , near Vaddahalli village, Shidlaghatta taluk, driver of the Bus bearing No.KA-40-6834 drove the same negligently,
dashed the same to the motorcycle , thereby caused the accident, caused injuries to the petitioner.
2. Petitioner took treatment at Government hospital, Chikkaballapura, Victoria hospital , Bengaluru.
3. Regarding the accident Dibburahalli police registered crime No.75/2022 .
4. As on the date of accident petitioner being aged about 30 years, used to earn Rs.20,000/p.m. by vending milk and by doing agriculture.

5. In response to the notice, respondents No.1 and 2 appeared through their respective advocates,
filed written statements denying the allegation regarding reason and mode of the accident , nature and consequence of the injuries suffered by the petitioner.

6. On the basis of the pleadings on 01.06.2023, this Authority has framed the following issues:
1. Whether the petitioner proves that on 27.05.2022 at about 07.45 a.m. on Talakayalabetta road, near Vaddahalli village, Shidlaghatta taluk, Chikkaballapura,
he met with an accident and sustained injuries, was due to actionable negligence act on the part of the driver of the bus bearing registration No.KA- 40-6834 as alleged?
2.
Whether the petitioner is entitled to compensation ? If so, how much and from whom?
3. What order?
7. On 01.06.2023, 03.07.2023, petitioner deposed as PW1 and produced 12 documents at Ex.P.1 to P.12.

On 31.07.2023 , 17.01.2024, 13.03.2024 petitioner produced the evidence of Nagaraja, Medical Record Technician at Victoria hospital , Bengaluru and Dr.Rajesh M.B. as PW2 and 3 and get produced 7 documents at Ex.P.13 to 19.

On 04.40.2024 , 22.07.2024 respondent No.1 insurance company produced the evidence of officer as RW1 and get produced 3 documents at Ex.R.1 to R.3.

sentences.text: I heard the arguments submitted on behalf of petitioner and respondent No.1 and perused the records.

9. On the basis of the record, my findings on the above issues are as under:
Issue No.1 ... Due to the negligent use of motorcycle bearing No.KA-40-H-7445 by the petitioner by keep sitting two persons on the pillion and negligent use of the Bus bearing No.KA-40-6834 at the ratio 20:80 accident taken place resulting in the injuries to the petitioner Issue No.2 ...

Petitioner is entitled to Rs.3,79,920/-
with current and future interest at 6% p.a as compensation from the respondents.
Issue No.3 ...

As per final order  for the following:-
 REASONS  10. Issue No.1 :- In the evidence petitioner stated that on 27.05.2022 at 7.45 a.m. when riding motorcycle bearing No.KA-40-H-7445 on Talakayabetta road, near Vadahalli village, Shidlaghatta taluk, driver of the Bus bearing No.KA-40-6834 drove the same negligently, dashed the same to the motorcycle , thereby caused the accident, caused injuries to the petitioner.
11. In the written statements respondents No.1 and 2 denied the allegation regarding reason and mode of the accident .
12. In the written statement respondent No.1 insurance company asserted that the petitioner who rode the motorcycle by keeping 2 persons on the pillion was the sole responsible for the accident.
13. In the cross-examination petitioner admitted that he was riding bike by keep sitting Ashwathappa and Kalavathi on the pillion.
Petitioner admitted that as per the sketch the place of accident is a curve area.
Petitioner denied the suggestion that the accident taken place in the cross road and in the cross area at the turning point vehicles coming from opposite direction is not visible.
Petitioner admitted that in the cross road one has to drive the vehicle by taking care and caution.
Petitioner denied the suggestion that by riding two wheeler in rash and negligent manner by keep sitting two persons on the pillion caused the accident.

Petitioner denied the suggestion that due to his rash and negligent act accident taken place.

In the evidence PW2 Nagaraja, Medical Record Technician at Victoria hospital produced the copy of police intimation, MLC register extract and case sheet at Ex.P.14 to P.16.
15.
In the evidence affidavit PW3 Dr. Rajesh M.B. stated nothing regarding reason and mode of accident.
16. In the evidence affidavit RW1 , officer of the insurance company , hear say witness reiterated the same facts as narrated in the written statement .

17. Ex.P.1 is the copy of FIR and complaint pertaining to crime No.75/2022 registered by Dibburahalli police on 29.05.2022 against the driver of the Bus bearing No.KA-40-6834 for having committed offence punishable under Section 279,337 of IPC regarding the accident taken place on 27.05.2022 at 7.30 a.m. between Bus bearing No.KA-40-6834 and motorcycle bearing No.KA-40-H-7445 resulting in the injuries to petitioner Narasimhamurthy, Ashwathappa and Kalavathi on the basis of the complaint presented by Ramesh N. S/o. Narayanappa.
Ex.P.2 is the copy of spot mahazar recorded on 30.05.2022.
Ex.P.3 is the vehicle seizure mahazar dated 30.05.2022.

Ex.P.4 is the copy of the sketch of place of accident in which it is noted that in curve area collision taken place between motorcycle and Bus .
18.
Ex.P.7 is the copy of wound certificate in which reason for the injuries are noted as RTA near Dibburahalli at 7.30 a.m. on 27.05.2022 between bus and two wheeler.

Ex.P.8 is the copy of the chargesheet filed by Dibburahalli police in crime No.75/2022 against Nataraja P.S., S/o.
Shankarappa , driver of Bus bearing No.KA-40-6834 for having committed offence punishable under Section 279,337, 338 of IPC .
In the police records name of the petitioner is noted as rider of the motorcycle, name of the petitioner Narasimhamurthy along with Ashwathappa , Kalavathi are noted as injured of the accident.
19. In this case there are no reasons to disbelieve the contents of the police records regarding reason and mode of the accident.

The evidence on record shows that in a curve area collision taken place between motorcycle on which 3 persons are sitting and Bus bearing No.KA-40- 6834 resulting in the injuries to 3 riders of the motorcycle.
20.

Hence, I have concluded that on 27.05.2022 at 7.45 a.m. on the curve road situated between Anemadagu and Talakayabetta road, near Vadahalli village, Shidlaghatta taluk, due to the use of motorcycle bearing No.KA-40-H-7445 by petitioner and negligent use of the Bus bearing No.KA-40-6834 by Nataraja, S/o. Shankarappa at the ratio 20:80 accident taken place between the motorcycle and bus resulting in the injuries to petitioner, rider of the motorcycle .
Hence, I answer issue No.1 accordingly.

21. Issue No.2: In the evidence petitioner stated that in the accident he has suffered right type 2 open distal femur fracture, right proximal 1/3rd of shaft of 1 st metacarpal fracture, right radial head undisplaced fracture, chest fracture of right middle epicondyle and other injuries, took first aid at District hospital , Chikkaballapura, then took treatment at Victoria hospital , Bengaluru as an inpatient by spending Rs.1,00,000/-.

sentences.text: 22. In the written statements respondents denied the allegation regarding nature and consequence of the injuries suffered by the petitioner.
23. In the cross-examination , petitioner denied the suggestion about non-spending of Rs.1,00,000/- for treatment and non-taking follow up treatment.
Petitioner admitted non-production of OPD slip regarding follow up treatment.
Petitioner denied the suggestion of non-earning of Rs.20,000/p.m. by vending milk and by doing agriculture.

24. In the evidence affidavit PW3 Dr.Ramesh stated that on 11.12.2023 when clinically examined the petitioner noticed that petitioner suffered permanent physical disability at 66% to right lower limb,
40% to the right upper limb and require to undergo further surgery to get removal of implants at the cost of Rs.75,000/-.

In the evidence PW3 produced clinical assessment proforma , x-ray and OP bill at Ex.P.17 to P.19.
25.
In the cross-examination PW3 submitted that he has neither treated the petitioner nor verified the case sheet, seen only wound certificate and discharge summary .
PW3 denied the suggestion that petitioner never suffered any of the complaint noted in para No.5 of his affidavit.
26. In the evidence affidavit RW1 officer of the insurance company, PW2 Medical Record Technician stated nothing regarding nature and consequence of the injuries suffered by the petitioner.

27. Wound certificate , medical bills, prescriptions , discharge card, case sheet and other medical documents shows that in the accident petitioner suffered right type II open fracture of distal femur ,
fracture of proximal 1/3rd of right 1st metacarpal, fracture of right radial head (undisplalced),
fracture of right medical epicondyle, took treatment at Victoria hospital , Bengaluru as an inpatient from 27.05.2022 to 20.06.2022 by spending Rs.40,900/-.

In the medical records age of the petitioner is noted as 36 years as on the date of accident .
28.
In this case petitioners has not produced any documentary evidence regarding his occupation and income.

As PW3 Dr.Ramesh stated that he neither treated the petitioner nor verified inpatient case sheet of the petitioner and submitted about verification of the wound certificate and discharge summary and in this case petitioner has not produced any type of evidence to show either decrease in the quantum of income or loss of income subsequent to the treatment taken for the injuries suffered in in the RTA , I have inferred that the oral evidence of Dr.Ramesh is insufficient to award compensation under the head of loss of future income.

29. Considering the nature of the injuries suffered by the petitioner , length, place and nature of the treatment taken by the petitioner , I assess Rs.1,40,000/- towards pain and sufferings , Rs.40,900/-
towards treatment charges, Rs.50,000/- towards conveyance, attendant and nourishment charges,
Rs.1,24,000/- (Rs.15,500x8) is assessed towards loss of income during treatment period ,
Rs.1,20,000/- towards loss of amenities and future unhappiness.

sentences.text:
Therefore, the total compensation assessed at Rs.4,74,900/-.
31.
In view of the finding recorded on issue No.1, 20% of the compensation amount is deducted towards negligence contributed by the petitioner.
Hence, I came to the conclusion that petitioner is entitle for compensation of Rs.3,79,920/- with current and future interest at 6% p.a. from the respondents as compensation.
32. In the written statement respondent No.1 insurance company admitted the subsistence of the policy with respect to the Bus bearing No.KA-40-6834 as on the date of accident .

In the reply submitted to the notice issued under Section 133 of IMV Act , the respondent No.2 owner of the bus noted the identification number of the driving licence possessed by Nataraja, S/o Shankarappa to drive the bus as on the date of accident.
Hence, it is clear that as on the date of accident, respondent No.2 owner of the Bus bearing No.KA-40-6834 has not violated any terms of the policy.

Hence, I came to the conclusion that respondents being the owner and insurer of Bus bearing No.KA-40-6834 are liable to pay compensation to the petitioner and an award is to be passed directing the respondent to pay compensation to the petitioners.

Hence, I answer issue No.2 accordingly and pass the following :
ORDER
The petition filed under Section 166 of IMV Act is hereby partly allowed.
The respondents shall either jointly or severally pay Rs.3,79,920/- with current and future interest at 6% p.a., to petitioner towards compensation.
The respondent No.1 being the insurer of the Bus bearing No.KA-40-6834 shall deposit the compensation amount with interest within 3 months from today.
After deposit of the compensation amount, entire compensation amount and interest may be released to the petitioner by crediting the same to his bank account directly.
Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/- .
Draw an Award accordingly.

(J.N.SUBRAMANYA) Chief Judge, Court of Small Causes & Member, Prl. M.A.C.T.
Bangalore.
